> Stack-specific standards for personal projects. Syncs to Directive standards + repo `CLAUDE.md`. Notation: **!** = MUST, **~** = SHOULD, **⊗** = MUST NOT.
## Swift / SwiftUI (ViLM)
- ! Respect size-class-driven navigation; validate layout on a physical iPhone before merging.
- ! Navigate to a record through the **shared helper**, never hand-rolled. Compact layout navigates by `navigationPath`; setting the selection alone is a no-op on a phone. *Added 2026-08-07: this rule exists to make the one above enforceable — it was broken twice in a day while the standard sat here unread.*
- ! Every `.sheet`-presented view ends in **`.macSheet`** or **`.macFormSheet`**. No raw `#if os(macOS)` + `.frame`. *macOS sheets size to content and **`List`**/**`ScrollView`**/**`LazyVGrid`** have no intrinsic height, so an unsized one renders as a title bar with no content area. Seven shipped like that once; the reason it recurred is that three conventions existed and no single search could establish the state.*
- ! Preserve existing defaults when adding seams for testability (default-preserving refactors).
- ~ A ⋯ menu holds at most **five top-level items**; group the rest into submenus, and assume every label wraps to three lines. *A menu is not a scrollable list. At an accessibility text size, seven items pushed **`Delete Video…`** off the bottom of the screen — present, rendered and unreachable.*
- ~ Keep views thin; push logic into testable models/view-models.
- ⊗ Don't introduce behavior changes inside a refactor commit.
## Testing
- ! Characterization tests before refactoring legacy code.
- ! Reproduce a reported or audited defect with a **failing test before changing code**. *Of an independent auditor's findings on 2026-08-06/07, five were false positives and every one proved first was real. A fix applied to a defect that was never demonstrated is a guess with a commit message.*
- ! A migration that adds a column names **every writer that must populate it**, or the column is not added. *`v29`** added provenance to six edge tables and only one writer filled it, leaving two thirds of the graph silently exempt from D7 while looking complete.*
- ~ Cover new runtime logic with unit tests; UI-only tweaks may rely on device validation.
## Documentation
> Added 2026-08-07. Every rule here is the result of a specific hour lost, not a preference.
- ! A tool added to Settings **ships with its in-app help entry in the same change**. *`HelpContent.settings`** enumerates the tools, so a missing entry is not an omission — it is a list claiming to be complete and failing. 16 of 22 tools had no entry when this was measured.*
- ! When a tool is renamed, its help entry is renamed with it. *`Import & Merge Graph`** was still documented as "Import and Merge Actor Library"; **`Delete Video`** pointed at a "Danger Zone" section removed three weeks earlier, and the operator went looking for it.*
- ! A README that describes how a repository is **consumed** must match how it is actually consumed. *The plugin README claimed a local package dependency; the app symlinks individual source files. Believing the README cost an hour of debugging invisible code.*
- ~ Re-read the README when an architectural epic lands. *The app README went five weeks without mentioning the graph, the plugin architecture or federation, and still listed shipped playlists as roadmap.*
## Source control & GitHub identity
Two GitHub accounts live on this machine: **`mranlett`** (personal — ViLM) and **`MattR3Ci`** (work — DealReview, Estimator, FinOps, and the `3Ci-Consulting` org). Git resolves *commit* identity automatically through the `includeIf` rule on the remote URL. **`gh`**** does not** — it holds one globally active account and applies it wherever you are standing.
- ! **Validate the active ****`gh`**** identity before every ****`gh`**** write, without exception.** Writes are `gh issue create/comment/close`, `gh pr create/merge/comment`, and `gh release`. This is a prerequisite, not a precaution: the active account is global state another session can change underneath you.
- ! **Validate before every push to a public repo**, and re-check after any `gh auth switch` — switching has silently reverted before.
- ⊗ **Never infer identity from the working directory, the git remote, or a command that succeeded a minute ago.** A correct remote proves nothing about which account is acting.
- ~ `gh: repo owner '…' has no authenticated account — falling back to the active one` is **expected** on this machine, not a misconfiguration. It is `gh` resolving an owner it holds no login for. ⚠️ It is also the sound of the guardrail being absent: the fallback picks the *active* account, which is right only by luck.
- ! **ViLM is public and personal.** A work-account write here is the Constitution Art. V breach in the direction people forget — the usual worry is personal code reaching work, and this is the reverse. Nothing about the repo will stop it.
- ⭐ The deeper operational detail — credential pins per owner, `useHttpPath`, why `Repository not found` is an identity failure rather than a missing repo — lives in the **3Ci Standards** under *Source control & GitHub identity*. It is machine-level and applies here too; it is documented there because that is where it was learned, and the two logs stay separate by design.
## Tooling
- ! Xcode project committed cleanly; no stray build artifacts.
- ! A standard that can be checked mechanically **gets a gate**; prose alone decays. *`~/.config/vilm-hygiene/check.sh`** (D9 vocabulary) and **`consistency.py`** (sheet sizing, help completeness) exist because the rules they enforce were all broken while written down.*
- ~ Node ≥ 20 + pnpm for any JS-based tooling in personal repos.
